recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit as-is; no follow-up source work is needed for FHIR-32551 unless OO intentionally changes the UDI carrier model in a future issue.
issue_request: FHIR-32551 asked why Device.udiCarrier.deviceIdentifier was 0..1 despite descriptions saying the DI is mandatory, and the accepted R5 resolution was to change the element to 1..1 because if udiCarrier exists the device identifier must be available.
initial_application: The source-changing application was commit 131f95eafec8ccb93611bc130755558068a3965d, which changed Device.udiCarrier.deviceIdentifier from min=0 to min=1 in source/device/structuredefinition-Device.xml. The Jira comment points to the FHIR-32551 PR/build application, and current blame still attributes the min=1 line to that source commit.
additional_context: Device is active in source/fhir.ini. Later same-area Device UDI issues, including FHIR-43063 and FHIR-47419, added Device.udiCarrier.deviceIdentifierSystem and clarified UDI wording while preserving the 1..1 cardinality. FHIR-20564 later rejected a cross-resource invariant between Device and DeviceDefinition UDI-DI values, which does not conflict with requiring deviceIdentifier inside each udiCarrier. Zulip and Confluence searches found no contrary community record.
reconciliation: No source change was needed. The current authoritative Device StructureDefinition has Device.udiCarrier.deviceIdentifier min=1 max=1, and build.fhir.org/device.profile.json reports the same cardinality.

related_jiras.note: Added Device.udiCarrier.deviceIdentifierSystem to clarify the namespace for the DI value without changing deviceIdentifier cardinality.
Clarified Device.udiCarrier and DeviceDefinition UDI wording while preserving Device.udiCarrier.deviceIdentifier as 1..1.
Rejected a cross-resource invariant for matching Device and DeviceDefinition UDI-DI values; it does not conflict with FHIR-32551's per-udiCarrier cardinality.
